steps.intro: Judge here: is each thing you asked for built the way you meant? Everything from round 6 is built. Each row's pictures sit in its Attachments card; its story is under "How this changed".

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: What you asked for, and what you got

calls.call: A row's pictures sit in an Attachments card at its foot, like Deliverables in a YouCoded chat.
calls.why: The viewer's arrows and picture strip are gone; a click opens one picture large.

reuse.note: Same folding card, with the deck's picture comments added.

trail.asked: i just need to have more space and a better surface to actually leave/manage comments and such and quickly scan through all of the changes at once
trail.built: A full-window viewer with a strip of every picture.
trail.said: the arrows that let me click between pictures are weird cuz they fully lose the context of the question

trail.asked: rows with images should have an "attachements" row/expandable card at the bottom kind of like the "deliverables" row/card in youcoded chats.

calls.call: Each row can carry its own story, round by round: what you asked, what was built, what you said.
calls.why: Open "How this changed" on any row of this list to see it.

trail.built: A History button opening a separate panel.
trail.said: You marked it Failed: you expected history woven into the deck.

trail.asked: maybe? but i think we need to refine the ui/ux of this further
trail.built: The trail on each row, plus New, Changed and Settled marks.

calls.call: A deck after its first round opens with a "Since last round" line: how many rows are new, changed and settled.
calls.why: Each count jumps to its rows. Settled rows fold shut at the bottom of a list.

calls.call: A picture or file path pasted or dropped into any comment box becomes a small pill under it.
calls.why: Pictures are saved beside the deck's answers, so I receive them.

reuse.note: Same pill shape and remove button.

trail.asked: i need to be able to attach/paste images/filepaths in these input boxes and have them work as pills like youcoded.

calls.call: A check row has a More line: what it does, what comes back, and why it is suggested for this build.
calls.why: Required on every check you can switch on or off.

trail.asked: i think these checks cards need to have more elaborate/expandable descriptiosn of what they actually entail and why they are/aren't recommended for the specific build

calls.call: A design or row can say which existing app parts it is built from, behind a small (i).
calls.why: You said this belongs in the deck, not in chat. The first and fourth rows here carry one.

calls.call: A wording page can carry a "Use it / Edit words" switch: open any dropdown in the running practice app, then switch to freeze it and retype its words.
calls.why: Not yet tried by a real hand, and it needs the practice app running, so the deck starts slower.

trail.asked: You picked the switch, and asked for the best and simplest way possible.
trail.built: The switch. Edits are remembered by the words you changed and the state the screen was in.

calls.call: Buttons follow the app's design guide: only Next and Done are filled; a chosen answer gets an outline and a tick.
calls.why: Open since round 4.

calls.call: A list shows a pill only once you changed it or moved past it. "Not reviewed" is gone.
calls.why: You called that pill confusing.

calls.call: The round-6 flow is written into the rule files every YouCoded chat reads.
calls.why: Explore first, "Here is how I understand this", drawn designs, walkthrough before and after, wording last, no contract.

calls.call: A background-only list has dashed rows and no pencils.
calls.why: Unchanged since round 6.

calls.call: A check can carry a Will run or Skip switch.
calls.why: Unchanged since round 6, apart from the larger pill on the next page.

steps.intro: Judge here: are the fixes right, and is anything I left alone wrong to leave? You asked for reviewers with no background. Three ran: two code reviewers and a first-time tester. One helper then fixed what they found.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Fixes you will see

calls.call: Pressing a row's pencil a second time no longer deletes your comment. A small × beside the comment removes it.
calls.why: The tester lost a comment this way with no warning.

calls.call: A status you change gets an outline and a "changed from" line. The pill is larger, with a small arrow.
calls.why: A changed row looked the same as an untouched one, and the pill read as a label.

calls.call: The option you pick gets a strong outline and a tick.
calls.why: It was a faint tint, the same look as "Recommended".

calls.call: The finish page says "Page 2, Question 3 of 3" and shows option names. A list you left alone reads "Left as listed".
calls.why: It showed internal labels and "Yes, build it" for lists you never touched.

calls.call: A background-only list is never counted as answered and never appears on the finish page.
calls.why: It was recorded as "Yes, build it".

calls.call: After Submit, every box is locked.
calls.why: One typing box still took text, which was then lost.

calls.call: A tiny accidental drag on a picture draws nothing.
calls.why: It left an empty, nearly invisible comment.

calls.call: At phone width the title has its own line and every button is tall enough to tap.
calls.why: The progress bar covered the title.

calls.call: A wording page opens zoomed to fit the window, with a count of your edits above the screen.
calls.why: On a short window the popup's foot is still cut off until you scroll.

calls.call: Two saves landing at once can no longer lose answers, and a late save can no longer undo your Submit.
calls.why: Found by the code reviewer; proven with a test of many saves at once.

calls.call: Page comments and status changes survive when the deck recovers from its backup copy.
calls.why: They were dropped; only answers came back.

calls.call: A saved screen is scrubbed of anything that can run or load from the internet before it enters a deck.
calls.why: A saved screen is a copy of a real page; it should be only words and layout.

calls.call: Recording stops if you close the tab mid-sentence or the voice helper fails.
calls.why: The microphone could stay open. Tested with a pretend microphone only.

calls.call: No web page outside this computer can read or change a deck's answers.
calls.why: The reviewer tried five ways in; all were refused.

calls.call: 16 automatic tests added, none removed: 445 in all, all passing.
calls.why: Each new test repeats one of the faults above and proves it stays fixed.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Found, and left alone

calls.call: Leaving a list page without touching it still accepts its rows.
calls.why: The tester called this surprising. You decided it in round 3: rows stand unless changed.

calls.call: The link stops working after Submit. The page now says "Sent. You can close this tab."
calls.why: Reopening is asked on the last page.

calls.call: Never tried: a real mouse on the Use it switch, a real microphone, a real phone, the light themes.
calls.why: I can only press buttons by script, and I do not record your microphone.

steps.intro: Judge here: which of these do you still want? You asked for a check of everything you said in six rounds against what exists. The rule files were corrected already. These are the rest.

steps.headline: Asked for or raised, and not done

calls.call: A status pill has no "Something else" choice.
calls.why: Round 5. Today: Passed, Failed, Unclear, Not done. A comment on the row is the workaround.

calls.call: No ready-made starting deck for "here are three drawn designs".
calls.why: Round 5. Chats build it from the questions starting deck each time.

calls.call: "Tests added and removed, in plain words" has no fixed place in the after-build walkthrough.
calls.why: Round 6. Today it is one row, as on the previous page.

calls.call: Your question about the app hosting deck links itself was never answered.
calls.why: Round 2. It is an app feature, so it would be an idea card, not part of this work.

calls.call: Three things I told you were not quite true: Notes "gone" (only on question decks), Related "built" (moved inside History), buttons "taken from the design guide" (matched by eye).
calls.why: Corrected here so the record is right.

steps.intro: Judge here: five decisions that block or shape what comes next.

steps.headline: May I tell the safety scanner to ignore five made-up ids?
steps.today: Thirteen saved steps of this work exist only on this computer. The scanner that guards every backup refuses to send them.
steps.problem: One old step holds five practice-app ids that look like passwords to the scanner. They are not secrets, and I am not allowed to rewrite saved history.
steps.proposal: Yes adds those five exact lines to the scanner's ignore list and backs everything up. Nothing else is loosened. No leaves the work on this computer only.

steps.path: The checks menu before a build
steps.headline: Which reviewers should be on by default?
steps.today: The new rules give every build a checks menu where each reviewer is suggested on or off. Nothing says which are normally on.
steps.checked: Counted across 32 past builds: the code reviewer made 241 findings, about two thirds accepted. About half the first-time tester's findings were noise. The grader changed nothing.
steps.problem: You asked to discuss this. Without a default, each chat guesses.
steps.proposal: Pick the default. You can still flip any switch on any build.

options.label: Code reviewer always on; the rest suggested per build
pros: Keeps the one that reliably finds real faults.
The tester runs only when there are new screens.
cons: I judge when the tester is worth it, and can judge wrong.

options.label: Code reviewer and first-time tester always on
pros: This round the tester found real faults the code reviewers missed.
cons: Slower builds, and about half its findings are noise I must sort.

options.label: Nothing on by default
cons: A fault like "second press deletes your comment" reaches you instead of a reviewer.

steps.path: A deck link opened again after Submit
steps.headline: What should reopening an answered deck do?
steps.today: The link dies on Submit. If I serve the deck again, it opens empty and your earlier answers are filed beside it.
steps.problem: The tester read the empty deck as lost answers, and could have answered twice.
steps.proposal: Pick what a reopened deck shows.

options.label: Your answers, still editable, with a line saying when you sent them
pros: You can correct one answer and send again.
cons: A second Submit replaces the first; the first is kept in a dated file.

options.label: Your answers, locked
cons: In August a locked deck read to you as "I can't click through".

steps.headline: On a phone, how should commenting on part of a picture start?
steps.today: Since this round's fixes a finger dragged across a picture draws a comment area. Before, a finger could not draw at all.
steps.problem: A swipe that starts on a picture now draws instead of scrolling the page. Not tried on a real phone.
steps.proposal: Pick how drawing starts on a touch screen. A mouse is unaffected.

options.label: Tap a "Comment on an area" button, then drag
Leave it: any drag draws
cons: On a page of large pictures, scrolling means aiming for the gaps.

options.label: No drawing on phones
cons: On a phone you describe the spot in words again.

steps.headline: Should I file two idea cards from earlier rounds?
steps.today: Two ideas came up and were never filed: a simple screen sketcher inside a deck whose sketch is handed to the chat, and the app hosting deck links itself.
steps.problem: Unfiled, they exist only in these decks.
steps.proposal: Pick which to file. Filing only records the idea; nothing is built.

options.label: File both
cons: Two more cards on the board.

options.label: Only the screen sketcher
pros: The one closest to your layout complaints.

options.label: Only app-hosted decks
pros: Would fix dead links at the root.
